question: If cot alpha=(P)/(Q), then find the value of (P cos alpha-Q sin alpha)/(P cos alpha+Q sin alpha) - (P²-Q²)/(P²+Q²)+3.
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Divide the first term by **sin α** to convert it into **cot α**.

(P cot α − Q) ÷ (P cot α + Q) = (P × (P/Q) − Q) ÷ (P × (P/Q) + Q) = (P² − Q²) ÷ (P² + Q²).

The total expression becomes [(P² − Q²) ÷ (P² + Q²)] − [(P² − Q²) ÷ (P² + Q²)] + 3.

The identical fraction terms cancel each other out, leaving only the constant.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** cot α = P/Q

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b5f04612c2fd5521439c848837fe7bdb5a4a0db5637beb65ecc727d3bfe7b27.png] 

**Formula Used:** cot α = cos α ÷ sin α

⇒ Let the expression be E = [(P cos α − Q sin α) ÷ (P cos α + Q sin α)] − [(P² − Q²) ÷ (P² + Q²)] + 3

⇒ Divide the numerator and denominator of the first term by sin α:

⇒ Term 1 = [P(cos α ÷ sin α) − Q(sin α ÷ sin α)] ÷ [P(cos α ÷ sin α) + Q(sin α ÷ sin α)]

⇒ Term 1 = (P cot α − Q) ÷ (P cot α + Q)

⇒ Substitute cot α = P/Q into Term 1:

⇒ Term 1 = [P × (P/Q) − Q] ÷ [P × (P/Q) + Q]

⇒ Term 1 = [(P² − Q²) ÷ Q] ÷ [(P² + Q²) ÷ Q]

⇒ Term 1 = (P² − Q²) ÷ (P² + Q²)

⇒ Substitute Term 1 back into the original expression E:

⇒ E = [(P² − Q²) ÷ (P² + Q²)] − [(P² − Q²) ÷ (P² + Q²)] + 3

⇒ E = 0 + 3 = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratio Identities

Fundamental identities include tan α = sin α ÷ cos α and cot α = cos α ÷ sin α = 1 ÷ tan α.

Pythagorean Identity

For any angle α, sin²α + cos²α = 1, which implies cos α = P ÷ √(P²+Q²) and sin α = Q ÷ √(P²+Q²) based on the right triangle.

Componendo and Dividendo Rule

If a ÷ b = c ÷ d, then (a + b) ÷ (a − b) = (c + d) ÷ (c − d). This is often used to simplify ratio-based trigonometric equations.</p
